source.title: Some Open Questions about Symplectic 4-Manifolds, Singular Plane Curves, and Braid Group Factorizations

accepted.question_text: Classify integral compact symplectic 4-manifolds up to symplectic equivalence when the fundamental group and the four numerical invariants c_1^2, c_2, c_1·[ω], and [ω]^2 are fixed. Here [ω] is the integral cohomology class of the symplectic form, c_1 and c_2 are the Chern classes of the tangent bundle, c_1^2 and c_2 are evaluated on the fundamental cycle, and c_1·[ω] and [ω]^2 are the corresponding cup-product pairings.

evidence.quote: Question 2.1. Can one classify all integral compact symplectic 4-manifolds with given values of (c_1^2, c_2, c_1 · [ω], [ω]^2) (and a given fundamental group)?

accepted.question_text: Given an arbitrary symplectic Lefschetz fibration over S^2, determine whether repeated fiber sum with a suitable collection of standard holomorphic Lefschetz fibrations must eventually produce a fibration that is isomorphic to a holomorphic one.

evidence.quote: Question 2.4. Does every symplectic Lefschetz fibration become isomorphic to a holomorphic fibration after repeatedly fiber summing with certain standard holomorphic fibrations?
Note added in proof: Questions 2.4 and 2.5 have now essentially been solved.

accepted.question_text: Let X_1 and X_2 be integral compact symplectic 4-manifolds with the same values of c_1^2, c_2, c_1·[ω], and [ω]^2. Determine whether there exists a finite collection of complex projective model surfaces such that, after repeatedly performing symplectic sums of X_1 and X_2 with the same chosen model surfaces, the resulting manifolds must become symplectomorphic.

evidence.quote: Question 2.5. Let X1, X2 be two integral compact symplectic 4-manifolds with the same (c_1^2, c_2, c_1 · [ω], [ω]^2). Do X1 and X2 become symplectomorphic after repeatedly performing symplectic sums with the same complex projective surfaces (chosen among a finite collection of model surfaces)?
Note added in proof: Questions 2.4 and 2.5 have now essentially been solved.

accepted.question_text: Let X_1 and X_2 be integral compact symplectic 4-manifolds with the same values of c_1^2, c_2, c_1·[ω], and [ω]^2. Determine whether X_2 can always be obtained from X_1 by a finite sequence of Luttinger surgeries, where a Luttinger surgery cuts out a neighborhood of an embedded Lagrangian torus and reglues it by a twist along a chosen essential loop so that the resulting 4-manifold remains symplectic.

evidence.quote: Question 2.6. Let X1, X2 be two integral compact symplectic 4-manifolds with the same (c_1^2, c_2, c_1 · [ω], [ω]^2). Is it always possible to obtain X2 from X1 by a sequence of Luttinger surgeries?

accepted.question_text: For fixed integers d, ν, and κ, classify symplectic plane curves in CP^2 of degree d having exactly ν nodes and κ cusps up to symplectic isotopy, meaning isotopy through symplectic curves that preserve the singularity data.
accepted.context_brief: symplectic isotopy of singular plane curves

evidence.quote: Question 3.5. Given integers (d, ν, κ), can one classify all symplectic curves of degree d in CP^2 with ν nodes and κ cusps, up to symplectic isotopy?

accepted.question_text: For fixed integers d, ν, κ, and N, classify all pairs (D, θ) up to admissible regular homotopy, where D is a symplectic degree-d curve in CP^2 with ν_+ positive nodes, ν_- negative nodes, and κ complex cusps satisfying ν_+ - ν_- = ν, and θ: π_1(CP^2 - D) → S_N is a compatible monodromy homomorphism. Here an admissible regular homotopy is a regular homotopy through such branch curves in which any creation of a node pair is allowed only when the two local geometric generators are sent by θ to transpositions on disjoint pairs of sheets.

evidence.quote: Question 3.11. Given integers (d, ν, κ, N), can one classify all pairs (D, θ) where D is a symplectic curve of degree d in CP^2 with ν+ positive nodes, ν− negative nodes and κ complex cusps, ν+ − ν− = ν, and θ : π1(CP^2 − D) → S_N is a compatible monodromy morphism, up to admissible regular homotopies?

The requirement for admissibility of a node creation operation is that the images by θ of these two geometric generators should be transpositions acting on disjoint pairs of elements (i.e., the branching phenomena above the two intersecting branches of D should occur in different sheets of the covering).

accepted.question_text: Let D_1 and D_2 be Hurwitz curves in the Hirzebruch surface F_n that represent the same homology class and have the same numbers of cusps and nodes. Suppose there are compatible monodromy morphisms θ_i: π_1(F_n - D_i) → S_N whose restrictions agree on the complement of some common fiber F that meets D_1 and D_2 in the same set. Determine whether there always exists a complex curve C in some Hirzebruch surface F_{n'} that is compatible with the given monodromy data and whose fiber sums D_1#C and D_2#C become isotopic as Hurwitz curves.

evidence.quote: Question 3.13. Let D1, D2 be two Hurwitz curves in F_n, representing the same homology class and with the same numbers of cusps and nodes. Assume that two compatible monodromy morphisms θ_i : π1(F_n − D_i) → S_N are given (i ∈ {1, 2}), and that there is a fiber F ⊂ F_n such that F ∩ D1 = F ∩ D2 and θ1|F − D1 = θ2|F − D2. Is there a complex curve C ⊂ F_n′, compatible with the given monodromy morphisms, such that the fiber sums D1#C and D2#C are isotopic to each other as Hurwitz curves?

accepted.question_text: Let D_1 and D_2 be symplectic plane curves in CP^2 with only positive nodes and cusps, having the same degree and the same numbers of nodes and cusps. Determine whether D_2 can always be obtained from D_1 by a finite sequence of braiding operations along embedded Lagrangian annuli in the complement, where such a braiding replaces two parallel local branches near the annulus boundary by a half-twisted configuration and corresponds on the branched cover side to Luttinger surgery.

evidence.quote: Question 3.17. Let D1, D2 be two symplectic curves with positive nodes and cusps in CP^2, of the same degree and with the same numbers of nodes and cusps. Is it always possible to obtain D2 from D1 by a sequence of braiding operations along Lagrangian annuli?
This construction is called “braiding” because, forgetting the S^1 factor, it replaces the trivial braid (−1, 1) × {±1/2} with the half-twist Γ̃.

accepted.question_text: For fixed integers d, ν, and κ, classify braid-group factorizations of the full twist Δ^2 in the Artin braid group B_d into τ = d(d - 1) - 2ν - 3κ half-twists, ν squares of half-twists, and κ cubes of half-twists, modulo Hurwitz moves and global conjugation.

evidence.quote: Question 4.1. Given integers (d, ν, κ), can one classify all factorizations of the central element Δ^2 of B_d into a product of τ = d(d − 1) − 2ν − 3κ half-twists, ν squares of half-twists, and κ cubes of half-twists, up to Hurwitz moves and global conjugation?

accepted.question_text: Fix a symmetric-group-valued morphism θ and let LB_d(θ) be the subgroup of the braid group B_d consisting of braids b such that θ ∘ b_* = θ, where b_* is the induced automorphism of the punctured-fiber fundamental group. Determine whether an analogue of Kharlamov-Kulikov stabilization holds inside LB_d(θ): namely, whether any two factorizations in LB_d(θ) of the same braid element, with the same numbers of factors of each type, become equivalent after appending enough copies of a suitable standard factorization and then applying Hurwitz moves.

evidence.quote: Question 4.4. Given a symmetric group valued morphism θ, does a statement similar to Theorem 4.3 hold for factorizations in LB_d(θ)?
Then the liftable braid group is LB_d(θ) = {b ∈ B_d, θ ◦ b_* = θ}.

Theorem 4.3 (Kharlamov-Kulikov). Let F and F′ be two factorizations of the same element in B_d, with the same numbers of factors of each type. Then there exists an integer n such that the factorizations F · (F_0)^n and F′ · (F_0)^n are equivalent under Hurwitz moves.

accepted.question_text: Let F and F' be factorizations of the same element of the braid group B_d, or of the liftable braid subgroup LB_d(θ), and assume they contain the same numbers of factors of each conjugacy type. Determine whether F and F' must always be equivalent under the combination of Hurwitz moves and partial conjugations by braids from B_d, respectively from LB_d(θ). A partial conjugation replaces a consecutive block of factors ρ_p, ..., ρ_q by b^{-1}ρ_p b, ..., b^{-1}ρ_q b when the product of that block commutes with b.

evidence.quote: Question 4.6. Are any two factorizations of the same element in B_d (resp. LB_d(θ)), with the same numbers of factors of each type, equivalent under Hurwitz moves and partial conjugations by elements of B_d (resp. LB_d(θ))?

Namely, given a factorization F with factors ρ1, . . . , ρr, integers 1 ≤ p < q ≤ r, and a braid b such that ∏_{p≤i≤q} ρ_i commutes with b, we can form a new factorization F′, with factors ρ1, . . . , ρ_{p−1}, (b^{-1}ρ_p b), . . . , (b^{-1}ρ_q b), ρ_{q+1}, . . . , ρ_r: the partial conjugate of F by b.
